problem.title: Implicit Type Coercion Invalidating B-Tree Indexes
problem.prompt: Customer lookup query passing string phone numbers to an indexed VARCHAR column via an ORM.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "SQL query parameters must strictly match column data types; implicit casting disables index traversal."
Production Hardening: Enforce strict schema-to-code type matching in ORM entity models, and configure database linting tools to flag queries containing type casts on indexed columns.
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Microburst → 100ms CFS Quota Used in 20ms → Kernel Freeze → 💥 P99 Latency Spike.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: The ORM passes the parameter as an integer or executes an implicit cast: 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE phone_number::int = 1234567890'. PostgreSQL cannot utilize the B-Tree index on phone_number , falling back to a full table scan and pegging CPU.
Breakdown Chain: Microburst → 100ms CFS Quota Used in 20ms → Kernel Freeze → 💥 P99 Latency Spike
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.
